regulatory_notes: The current Chapter 2.11 contains standards 2.11.1 to 2.11.9, with 2.11.6 omitted.

The chapter PDF currently published in FSSAI's chapter-wise compendium does not print a chapter version/date; PMSV therefore records it as the current consolidated chapter rather than inventing a version number.

Special dietary food with low sodium content under 2.11.9 is a process/compositional overlay, not a standalone FoSCoS product. FoSCoS guidance instructs the FBO to select the corresponding underlying food category and additionally comply with the low-sodium standard.
Historical references in Chapter 2.11 to the former Packaging and Labelling Regulations, 2011 are not treated as the current labelling instrument; current Labelling and Display Regulations apply.

common_rules.text: Applicable products must comply with current Food Safety and Standards (Contaminants, Toxins and Residues) requirements.
Current Food Safety and Standards (Labelling and Display) Regulations apply in addition to product-specific declarations.
Food additives and processing aids are permitted only where allowed by the applicable product standard and relevant FSSAI appendices/regulations.

overlay_rules.name: Special dietary food with low sodium content
overlay_rules.applicability: Apply in addition to the underlying standardized food identity; do not treat as a standalone product identity.

conditions: Processed without addition of sodium salts.
Sodium content is not more than one half of the comparable normal product as consumed.
Processed without addition of sodium salts.
Sodium content is not more than one half of the comparable normal product as consumed.

label_rules: Use the description 'low sodium' or 'very low sodium' only when the relevant 2.11.9 conditions are met.
Declare sodium content to the nearest 5 mg per 100 g and additionally per specified serving as normally consumed.
Declare average carbohydrate, protein and fat per 100 g and energy value.
If the salt substitute contains potassium salts, declare total potassium as mg cation per 100 g of food as normally consumed.
Declare salt equivalent as NaCl per serving and total NaCl in the pack.
Declare special storage conditions where applicable.
overlay_rules.foscos_note: FoSCoS guidance states Special dietary food with low sodium content is not listed as a standalone product; select the corresponding food category and comply additionally with this standard.

standards.name: Baking Powder
standards.definition: Combination capable under baking conditions of yielding carbon dioxide, consisting of sodium bicarbonate, acid-reacting material and starch or another neutral material.
optional_neutral_materials: Edible starches from cereals, roots and tubers
permitted_acidulants: Potassium bitartrate / potassium hydrogen tartrate (cream of tartar)

standards.name: Catechu (Edible)
standards.definition: Dried aqueous extract prepared from heartwood of Acacia catechu.

composition.parameter: Loss on drying at 100°C to constant weight
Ash insoluble in HCl on dry basis
Ash insoluble in dilute HCl — Bhatti Katha

standards.identity_test: 1% aqueous solution with 0.1% ferric ammonium sulphate gives dark green; addition of sodium hydroxide changes it to purple.

standards.name: Gelatin
standards.definition: Purified product obtained by partial hydrolysis of collagen derived from skin, white connective tissues and bones of animals.
quality_rules: Colourless or pale yellowish and translucent; sheets, flakes, shreds or coarse-to-fine powder.
Very slight characteristic odour/taste but not objectionable.

standards.name: Silver Leaf (Chandi-ka-warq)
quality_rules: Food-grade silver leaf shall be a sheet of uniform thickness, free from creases and folds.
It shall not be manufactured using any material of animal origin at any stage.

composition.parameter: Ash insoluble in dilute HCl on dry basis

standards.name: Carob Powder
standards.definition: Powder obtained from roasted pods of carob (Ceratonia siliqua) and free from husk.

standards.name: Dietary Fibre (Dextrin-soluble fibre)
standards.definition: Glucose polymer of natural origin produced by dextrinification of acidified starch followed by purification, containing digestible and indigestible linkages.
source_rules: Ingredient source (wheat/maize) shall be non-genetically modified.
permitted_use_at_gmp: Flakes and ready-to-eat dry breakfast cereals
Salad dressing or toppings and spreads
Table-top fibre as filler or carrier and cereals
Bakery products including biscuits, cookies, bread, cake mixes and pastries
Other products where dextrin is allowed under the regulations
standards.historical_claim_text_note: The Chapter 2.11 compendium reproduces legacy dietary-fibre claim thresholds from the former Packaging and Labelling Regulations. PMSV stores them for traceability but does not use them as the current claim engine without validation against current Advertising and Claims/Labelling rules.

legacy_claim_thresholds.text_as_printed: not less than 3 g/100 g or 1.5 g/100 kcal and not more than 6 g/100 g or 3 g/100 kcal
